Requirements: R-1, R-2, R-4, R-14
Plan row: TS-8

Obligations: OB-10, OB-11. Q4 a: the feature is wanted; the Project dropdown stands in for a "Change project" button. Q3 b: Move only, no mode choice is expected.

## Given
- An integration in the source project; a target project the user administers.
- The edit page of the integration is open.

## When
Decision table (one parameterized flow):
1. P-changed-confirm: select the target in the Project dropdown, press Save, press Confirm in the modal.
2. P-changed-cancel: select the target, press Save, press Cancel in the modal.
3. P-unchanged: change only the alias, press Save.
4. After each, read the integration by id and the project lists through the API.

## Then
1. The Project dropdown is enabled on the edit page of an existing integration (R-1, R-2).
2. P-changed-confirm and P-changed-cancel: pressing Save with a changed project shows a modal titled "Change integration project?" before any request is sent.
3. P-changed-cancel: no save request is made and the API shows the integration still in the source, fields unchanged.
4. P-changed-confirm: the API read-back shows the integration in the target project and absent from the source.
5. P-unchanged: no modal appears and the alias is saved.

## Self-probe notes
- Discriminating input: project changed versus unchanged, confirm versus cancel; a modal that is cosmetic (saves regardless) fails Then 3.
- Persistent state is read through the API, independent of the UI toast. Cancel proof needs the request count (route interception) or the persistent unchanged read-back; both are listed in Then 3.
- R-2 is satisfied by the dropdown per Q4 a. Whether dependents are named in the modal text is not asserted: R-14 gives the title only.
- R-4 (selectable permitted target) is checked here only as "a permitted target can be selected"; options for a non-admin are TC-012.
